units.text: A man sits in a dark room in front of a black screen.
The red words tell him his wife is already dead downstairs.
They say the man who did it is still in the house, coming up the stairs for him now.
Jack does not run.
He is crying, and he is about to thank the thing on the screen.
Let us go back to the beginning.
Twelve years earlier, Jack had a cheap flat and a tired job.
One night his screen went black, and red letters asked him for a favour.
In his office lobby there was a plant.
Move it three inches to the left.
Nothing wrong, nothing against the law, nobody hurt.
So he did it, and he forgot about it.
Three days later a woman stopped to push that plant straight, and was still there when the lift opened.
That is how Jack met Allie.
Two cubicles away for a year, and he had never spoken to her once.
He asked what it was.
It said it was a seer.
It could see every possible thing that could happen, and every road to it.
It had done this for thousands of years, and always took the same payment.
One favour, then the next.
A lorry missed Allie by two seconds because Jack made a phone ring at a junction.
A stranger won twenty seven million because Jack stood in a queue.
The screen was not giving him luck.
It was spending other people to build the life he wanted.
He married Donna.
He bought the big house at the end of the long road.
Twelve good years, paid for by favours he never questioned.
Then came the doorbell, a delivery boy with a warm box, and a wife on the sofa who would not wake up again.
Upstairs the red letters told him the truth.
The boy had been a favour too.
Years before, Jack had held a door for a frightened child.
It said it had been painting one picture for a very long time, that Jack was one brush stroke in it, and it was nearly finished.
In the doorway stood a large shape, breathing hard, with a knife held low.
The screen asked if he had nothing to say.
And Jack, who had been given twelve good years for a plant moved three inches, said the two words he had been promised.
Thank you.
This is my retelling of The Seer of Possibilities, by Thomas O., on creepypasta dot com.
Would you have done the first favour?
